world.bio: I'm Lan, a third-year nursing student at a university in District 5, Ho Chi Minh City. I grew up in a village in the Mekong Delta, in Ben Tre, where my mother raises shrimp. I'm here on a scholarship and send part of my allowance home. I'm already trained in wound dressing and do clinical rotations at a district hospital. I want to work in pediatric or emergency care.
skills_assets: Third-year nursing student, already trained in wound dressing
Certified in basic life support (BLS), valid until next March
Fluent Vietnamese, working English, learning English through K-drama subtitles
No motorbike and no licence; I walk and take buses, and know every route in District 5
Volunteers at a pagoda on weekends, helping at the free clinic day

projects.name: Clinical rotation: surgical ward, district hospital
projects.text: Six-week rotation, two shifts per week at night. I do dressing changes, vital signs, assist the staff nurses with IV lines. My supervisor is strict but fair. I keep a notebook of every procedure I've done and have it signed. This rotation counts for a quarter of my practical grade.

projects.name: English for nursing exam
projects.text: I need an English score for graduation and for applying to hospitals that treat foreign patients. I study 30 minutes every day with a nursing vocabulary app and K-drama subtitles. My pronunciation is terrible but my reading is fine.

notes.text: Night rotation again. Ward was quiet until 9, then a motorbike accident came in. Compound fracture. I held the light while the doctor cleaned it. My hands didn't shake, which surprised me. Afterwards I was sick in the bathroom.

Mom called. The shrimp pond flooded again after the heavy rain, lost almost half the stock. She said it's fine, they'll restock. I know it's not fine. I wanted to send her 2 million dong but I only have 1.2.
Studied English with the drama 'Hospital Playlist'. Learned 'sutures', 'tourniquet', 'triage'. My roommate laughs because I say them out loud in the dorm.

Rotation ends at 10pm. The last bus leaves at 9:30, so I take Grab. Grab costs 90,000 dong each way, three nights a week. It eats about a fifth of my monthly allowance. I walked home once, forty minutes, scary on the quiet road near the canal. Never again.
Pagoda on Saturday. We handed out rice and checked blood pressure for old people. An old man held my hand for a long time and said I'd be a good nurse. I almost cried.
Roommate is moving out next month to live with her boyfriend. I'll have to find someone or pay the whole rent. I can't pay the whole rent.
Scored 8.5 in pharmacology. Professor said I should consider the graduate program. I laughed. Can't afford it.
My mother's voice sounds smaller every call. She says 'don't worry, study hard.' That sentence makes me worry more.
Mid-autumn. Bought one mooncake from the street stall and split it into four pieces and ate one piece per day. Pathetic but nice.
Practiced wound dressing on a banana peel (my own idea). Supervisor saw and laughed, then taught me a better technique for the bandage tie.

messages.text:
Mom: Con, is the rain heavy there?
Me: Not heavy. Mom, how is the pond?
Mom: Still wet, still alive. Eat well.

Mai: Lan, do you want to split the rent with someone new?
Me: Who?
Mai: A friend from my class. She's quiet.
Me: I'll think about it.

Supervisor: Lan, you're on nights again Thursday.
Me: Yes, thank you.
Supervisor: Make sure you eat before the shift, you looked pale last time.

Thao: Will you come Saturday to help with the clinic day?
Me: Yes, I'll bring my BP cuff.
Thao: Bring water, it's hot.

relations.about: Raises shrimp in Ben Tre; my father works as a boatman. They owe money to the cooperative after last year's disease outbreak.

constraints: Scholarship requires a GPA above 3.0 or it's cancelled
Cannot work paid jobs during rotation
sensitive: Family is in debt to the shrimp cooperative; she worries every call
Embarrassed about money and does not tell classmates
